question.prompt: What is the maximum value of \(f(x)=x^2-2x\) on \([0,3]\)?

solutions.explanation: \(f'(x)=2x-2\), with a stationary point at \(x=1\). Since \(f(0)=0\), \(f(1)=-1\), and \(f(3)=3\), the maximum value is \(3\).
solutions.title: Derivative and endpoint test

solutions.explanation:
Completing the square makes the size of \(x-1\) control the function value:
\[
f(x)=(x-1)^2-1.
\]
For \(0\le x\le3\), we have \(-1\le x-1\le2\), so \((x-1)^2\le4\). Thus \(f(x)\le3\). Equality occurs at \(x=3\), where \(f(3)=3\), so the maximum value is \(3\).
solutions.title: Completing the square
